reviewed_by: Claude #1094 implementer; the defect was independently reproduced with real supervisor and API worker processes by a separate Claude validator (issues/private-channel/validation.md) before any fix; an independent diff review is still required before merge
reason: Backend fix for #1094. The stable listener signs every public request onto the private runtime channel before the API worker authenticates its caller, and each one spent a nonce from a bounded per-lane replay set (256 control / 4096 read and work per 30 s), so anonymous traffic made the operator's Stop and approval decision return 429; anonymous unfinished uploads also held the 16 control (or 64 shared read/work) forwarding connections so operator requests got 503. Senders now number nonces per receiver key, lane and transport inside a random epoch and receivers check a sliding window per epoch, so volume is never refused; requests that present no recognised credential travel in their own connection pool and never on the control lane. Python: the private-channel gate and proxy file (numbering, replay and stale refusal, legacy nonce sets), the stable-listener file (credential classification, recognised-device cache, and a real supervisor + API worker process test of a 300-request anonymous burst and 20 control + 70 work-path unfinished uploads while operator Stop, decision and read stay answered), and the routing file whose control-lane assertion changed.
exclusions: No UI, frontend, native or Playwright changes: the operator-visible result (Stop and approval answered instead of 429/503) is proven by the real-process supervisor test and a scratch real-Core probe recorded in the PR. Execution-worker and project-worker private channels use the same gate but only receive already-authenticated traffic; test_runtime_processes.py, test_execution_worker_process.py and test_runtime_worker_features.py exercise those senders unchanged and are excluded as process-heavy suites outside the changed admission logic. Python 3.12 only.
